claim: A third deed read inwardly: after the cities as impurities (343), the burning of Kama becomes the yogi's restraint of the mind and the linga's way.

905 calls the poet's sorrow ஒருநாள் பிரிவதும் அரிதாய்ச் சுழல்படும் ஒழியாத் துயர், a whirling grief in which even one day's parting is hard to bear. Kural 1269 says ஒருநாள் எழுநாள்போல் செல்லும் for those who wait for a distant lover's return. The Thiruppugazh borrows the parted lover's measure of a single day, but names it as the bondage to be escaped (தவிரேனோ).

Thiruppugazh 47 asks Murugan gently to bring to shore one who drowns in a sea of pleasure among women, and to give his golden anklets (இன்பக் கடலூடே அமிழுவேனை மெத்தென ஒரு கரைசேர்த்து அம்பொற் றண்டைக் கழல்தாராய்). Kural 10 says only those who reach the Lord's feet swim the great sea of births (பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் நீந்துவர் ... இறைவன் அடிசேராதார்). The song turns the sea of births into the sea of pleasure, and like the Kural makes the feet the way across.

1882 says the land where a 'சிவயோகி ஞானி' dwells gains knowers and good order and becomes the higher world. 1913 says that if the jnani's body is kept in a cave-tomb, kings and all who live on the earth 'அந்தமில் இன்ப அருள்பெறுவாரே'. 1913 extends 1882's blessing of place from the living sage to his tomb.

Both show an old man with failing speech or teeth and a staff whose eyes are still on desire. The Naladiyar says such a man has no way to safety; 1166 is the old man's own confession and still hopes his mind will turn to song.

தரியாத போத கத்தர் குருவாவ ரோரொ ருத்தர்
தழலாடி வீதி வட்ட மொளிபோத ஞான சித்தி
குருநாடி ராச ரிக்கர் துரியோத னாதி வர்க்க
குலையாமல் நீதி கட்டி யெழுபாரை யாள விட்ட

மதுரா புரேசர் மெய்க்க அரசாளு மாறன் வெப்பு
claim: 575 asks to gain the path of Sivayoga in the line of the teaching guru (உபதேச குருபர சம்ப்ரதாயமொடு ஏயும் நெறி). 573 asks whether knowledge handed on by gurus one after another, with japa, fire offerings and breath restraint, can be a refuge (தஞ்சமாமோ), and says it would be so only if Siva gave it (தழலாடி ... ஞான சித்தி தருமாகில்). Read together, 573 puts a condition on the guru-lineage 575 trusts: the teaching avails when the Lord gives it; this depends on the uncertain reading of தரியாத போதகத்தர்.

2526 says the siddhas have seen Siva and, steeped in pure and impure, remain unsteeped (தோய்ந்தும் தோயாதவர்), of the nature of Sadasiva. 127 says they remained having become Sivam and everything (இருந்தார் சிவமாகி எங்குந் தாமாகி), watching all of Siva's acts. Both describe the siddha who has become Siva and still remains among things.
The Kural calls number and letter (எண், எழுத்து) the eyes of living beings; Tirumular makes the Supreme their maker and goes on to the eye that takes things in. Learning's two eyes become his gift.

436 describes poets who liken the rich to the kalpaka tree, the rain cloud and Pari and make thieving poems for money (திருட்டுக் கவிகள் பாடி). 271 renounces poets who liken base patrons to the pouring cloud and the wish-tree and who steal and twist old verses (பழைய மொழியைத் திருடி நெருடிக் கவிபாடி). Both name patron-praise as theft; 436 adds that the gold so earned goes to the courtesans.

1637 says the worldly who listen to and serve the people of tapas (பணி கேட்கின்) may come face to face with Nandi. Kural 443 says the rarest of rare things is to cherish the great and make them one's own (பெரியாரைப் பேணித் தமராக் கொளல்). Tirumular carries the Kural's counsel on choosing great companions into the spiritual sphere, where service of the tapasvins becomes the way to the Lord.

973 asks that he not, desiring women's shoulders (மடவார் தோள் விரும்பி), cross the bounds (வரம்பு கடந்து) and waste away. Kural 919 calls the soft shoulders (மென்தோள்) of women who keep no bounds (வரைவிலா) the mire where base men sink. The song turns the Kural's women without bounds into the man who crosses his own.
An image without life: the Kural likens the unlearned man's good looks to a clay doll; Tirumular makes the Lord a stone cow, giving no milk, to those who neither recite nor realise him.

344 says at the sacrifice of three fires the gods did not know who Hara was, and the killing arose from within that fire (அத்தீயின் உள்ளெழுந்தன்று கொலையே). 353 tells the same event at Daksha's sacrifice: when the Lord grew angry fire burst through the flame (வெந்தழல் ஊடே புறப்பட) and the gods' worship broke off. One episode appears in two chapters, the deeds of Siva and Daksha's sacrifice, both placing the destruction inside the sacrificial fire.

claim: 861 calls the poet one who does not melt like wax (மெழுகென உருகாவனார்), tangled in mala and maya, and asks the Lord to come and give Siva-jnana teaching. Tirumanthiram 272 says that no fierce penance reaches the gem, only those who melt with love and soften within (அன்போடு உருகி அகங்குழைவார்க்கு அன்றி). Both make melting the condition; the song counts its absence among the poet's faults and asks grace to supply what he cannot.
